method: Assistant visually inspected all thirty source/0.11.18/PR triptychs plus the six 600-DPI crops, both opaque-gradient controls, resolution-control pages 1, 2, 4, and the old/PR ink-channel planes. This is specimen inspection, not a visual review of every full-book page.
observations: Text edges improve on eligible split pages; the callout ink control has pure K dark pixels in the PR specimen.
Combined page 4 reveals words under the foreground cover; combined and isolated page 13 remove the foreground tint from text.
Original-font effects pages checked are pixel-identical old versus PR, including retained cover/tint appearance, with no live-text gain.
Brick detail softens at 300 DPI; photographic plate detail changes less. Rules lose vector edges, while ordinary text remains crisp.
Tested gradient fallback keeps appearance at the cost of live text; opaque repeating gradient still distorts, while opaque conic paints in both versions.
